plain: A symbol that stands for a quantity whose value may vary or is not yet known.
A mathematical phrase made from numbers, symbols and operations; unlike an equation, it does not assert that two sides are equal.
A statement that two expressions have the same value.
A quantity represented by a symbol when its value has not yet been determined.
A value, or set of values, that makes a statement such as an equation true.
A straight path that continues in both directions; in a coordinate graph, a linear equation in two variables can describe one.
Two or more equations considered together; a shared solution must make every equation true.
A rule that assigns exactly one output to each allowed input.
A value supplied to a rule or process.
The value produced by applying a rule to an input.
A visual display of values or relationships, often using points on coordinate axes.
The change in vertical position divided by the change in horizontal position along a straight line.
The point where a graph meets an axis; in y=mx+b, b is where the line crosses the vertical axis.
A function whose graph is a straight line.
The small raised number that tells how many times a base is used as a factor.
The number repeatedly multiplied in a power; in 2³, the base is 2.
A change where the amount increases by the same factor over equal steps, rather than by the same added amount.
A change where the amount is multiplied by the same fraction over equal steps.
A count of how many times a base must be multiplied by itself to reach a positive value.
The number whose repeated multiplication is counted by a logarithm.
A compact way to say that a sequence of terms should be added.
The operation of adding several values together.
A comparison of two quantities by division.
A ratio expressed as a number of parts per hundred.
The total of a list divided equally among the number of values in the list.
For a point on the unit circle, the sine of its angle is the point's vertical coordinate.
For a point on the unit circle, the cosine of its angle is the point's horizontal coordinate.
A measure of rotation or the opening between two directions.
A circle of radius one centered at the origin of a coordinate plane.
An angle unit based on how much arc length is swept out on a circle.
A unit for angles where one complete turn is divided into 360 equal parts.
A small character written below a symbol to label it or distinguish it from related symbols.
A small character written above a symbol; it may indicate a power, but context matters.
A quantity with components; depending on context, it can represent direction and magnitude or simply an ordered list.
The relation that says an object belongs to a collection.
A symbol such as 'for every' or 'there exists' that tells how broadly a statement applies.
A number from zero to one used to describe uncertainty under a stated model.
llm: A language model represents a next-token distribution with probabilities over its vocabulary.

plain: The set of token IDs a particular language model can predict as its next output.
llm: The next-token probabilities sum to one over the model's output vocabulary.

plain: The limit on how much tokenized input and generated text a model can use in one context.
llm: Prompt and generated tokens are subject to a model's context-window limit.

plain: A simplified computational unit that combines inputs using weights and a bias, then may apply an activation.
llm: A feed-forward network can be described as layers of learned transformations and nonlinear activations; a single weighted sum is only a simplified piece.

plain: A sum in which each input is multiplied by its own weight before the results are added.
A learned offset added to a weighted sum.
llm: Some neural-network layers include a learned bias term; architectures may omit biases in particular layers.

plain: The logarithm of a probability; it is often used because multiplying probabilities becomes adding their logarithms.
llm: Language-model sequence scores and training objectives commonly use log probabilities.

plain: A measure of how well one probability distribution assigns probability to outcomes drawn from another distribution.
llm: Next-token prediction is commonly trained by minimizing cross-entropy, equivalently maximizing token likelihood under the usual setup.

plain: A unit of information corresponding to a choice between two equally likely possibilities.
llm: Bits per token can describe average information or coding cost; the exact measure depends on the evaluation setup.

plain: A language-model evaluation quantity obtained by exponentiating average cross-entropy in nats; lower values indicate better predictions on the evaluated data.
llm: Perplexity is defined from average token cross-entropy, but comparisons depend on tokenization and evaluation data.

plain: A learned number that scales the contribution of an input in a calculation.
A model made from connected layers of computations whose weights are learned from data.
A neural-network component that applies successive transformations to its input, with data flowing in one direction through that component.
A model that assigns probabilities to text sequences or predicts text units from context.
llm: Autoregressive language models commonly predict a distribution over the next token given prior tokens.

plain: A unit in a model's text representation; it may correspond to a word, part of a word, punctuation, or another piece.
The process of converting text into the token units used by a model.
A rule assigning probabilities to possible outcomes, with the total probability equal to one.
A function that converts a finite list of scores into positive values that sum to one.
A neural-network architecture for sequences built from layers of learned transformations; many language models use this architecture.
A number found by multiplying corresponding vector components and adding those products; geometrically it also reflects alignment.
A representation added or applied so a sequence model can use information about token positions.
llm: The original Transformer paper introduced sinusoidal positional encodings as one option; later models use varied approaches.

plain: A function applied to a computation in a neural network, often to provide a nonlinear transformation.
A number measuring how poorly a model's predictions match a chosen target under a specified objective.
A unit of information associated with natural logarithms.
A boundary in an input space where a classifier changes its predicted category.
A representation that maps an item, such as a token, to a vector of numbers.
A field focused on methods that let computer systems learn patterns or useful behavior from data.
